sections.content: How many people stayed in Glastonbury after gaining qualifications?

Glastonbury is a small town in the South West. Glastonbury does not have its own university.

Glastonbury has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Glastonbury ended up with:

  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 420 state-school pupils from Glastonbury who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 110 (26%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 145 (35%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Glastonbury to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Glastonbury's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Glastonbury in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Glastonbury move to?

Of Glastonbury's graduates, 65 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Glastonbury's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 65 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 30 of those qualified non-graduates (46%) were living fairly locally, in the Street and Wells travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Glastonbury's GCSE cohort:

  • 40 graduates left the South West

In 2018 to 2019, 50% of qualified non-graduates living in Glastonbury had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 160 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Glastonbury, compared with the 145 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, 50% of qualified (level 3+) non-graduates in Glastonbury had also lived there when they sat their GCSEs, while 50% had moved there from elsewhere.
